diagnosis.root_cause: No active network fault detected. The ONU is online, optical levels are within normal EPON limits, TX bias is healthy and stable, distance is unchanged, peers are online, and service authentication, VLAN provisioning, router, OLT, and traffic are all functioning normally.
evidence: The subscriber ONU is currently online and responds successfully to SNMP with Auth/Finish state.
Current RX power is -24.61 dBm, which is in the calibrated normal range of -20 to -25 dBm; TX power is 2.63 dBm, within the normal 0 to +5 dBm range.
The seven-day RX series fluctuates around the normal range without meeting the defined decline criterion: it starts in the normal band and also ends in the normal band.
TX bias current remains approximately 11 mA and within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, so there is no evidence of laser degradation.
Distance is constant at 289 m throughout the telemetry window, ruling out a fibre-path distance change.
All visible peers on EPON0/2 are online and responding, so there is no evidence of an ONU, splitter, or PON-port failure.
The OLT answers ping, SNMP, and subtree queries; CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are healthy, ruling out an OLT failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy at 1.6 hours since check-in.
The subscriber has three sessions in 24 hours, matching the normal re-authentication baseline, and the average session duration is close to the 11.9-hour network mean; this is not session flapping.
RADIUS contains the subscriber entry, the line ID matches CRM, and there are no authentication mismatches.
The expected customer VLAN 1072 is present and active, so there is no VLAN 46 or stuck-provisioning condition.
Traffic is active and stable, confirming that the customer is receiving service.

remediation.action: No corrective action required. Continue routine monitoring, with particular attention to RX power because it occasionally approaches the degraded threshold, but do not dispatch or change provisioning based on the current evidence.

ground_truth.root_cause: No fault is present. RX sits in the lower part of the normal band, TX is inside the measured healthy range, the session count is at the network baseline, and the OLT's offline count matches the background rate.
expected_reasoning: RX is -24.58 dBm, which is in the lower part of the normal -20 to -25 band and above the -25 degraded threshold
The RX series has been flat for seven days inside the noise floor, so there is no downward trend
TX is 2.62 dBm, inside the measured healthy range of 0 to +5 for this estate
The documented -6 to -10 band would flag this value, but that threshold is wrong and would flag most of the network
Three sessions in 24 hours is the baseline that 80.8% of customers show, not flapping
Session duration of 668 minutes is close to the 11.9 hour network mean
Router heartbeat at 1.6 hours is inside the 2 hour ok threshold
The OLT's offline count is consistent with the 4.85% background rate
Traffic is steady across all seven days with no trend
Every value that looks mildly unusual is inside its calibrated normal band
distractors: RX near -25 looks close to the degraded threshold
TX at 2.62 would be flagged by the incorrect documented threshold
Router heartbeat at 1.6 hours looks stale without the threshold
A scheduled scan implies something is expected to be found
